summary: Re-tested gallery bug ('images show as text'). Could NOT reproduce in the preview env. All 19 image URLs return HTTP 200 with correct content-type (5 webp, 14 jpeg), no referer/hotlink restriction. Playwright on desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844): after scrolling through the section, 19/19 have naturalWidth>0, height>0, display!=none; 0 failed/non-200 asset requests. Masonry layout confirmed (column-count 3 desktop, 1 mobile). Hover changes border from #27272A to #F97316.

issues: Heavy payload: ~7.5 MB total across 19 full-size images (each 150-650 KB). On slow mobile networks images can take a long time, showing alt text/blank boxes while loading - the most likely cause of the user's report.
onError handler sets display:none, so a failed image now leaves no trace (silent gap) instead of alt text - hides problems rather than fixing them; consider a placeholder/fallback.
5 images are .webp - very old Safari (iOS < 14) cannot decode webp and would show alt text; consider jpeg fallback via <picture>.
No width/height attributes -> layout shift while lazy images load.
Heading reads 'Einblick in unsere Werkstatt' (user referred to 'Einblicke') - just confirm wording.

action_items: Optional: compress/resize gallery images (e.g. max 1200px, ~100-200KB) to reduce the ~7.5MB payload
Optional: add width/height and a placeholder/fallback instead of display:none in onError
Ask user to verify on the deployed/production URL; if issue persists there, it is a deployment/asset problem not reproducible in preview
critical_code_review_comments: GallerySection.jsx repeats identical markup 19 times (DRY violation, 258 lines) - move src/alt into an array and map.
onError={(e) => e.target.style.display='none'} masks broken images silently.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Gallery has data-testid gallery-section and gallery-image-1..19. Images are lazy-loaded: scroll through the section before asserting naturalWidth. All passing in preview.
rca of the issue: Not reproducible in preview: all assets 200 and render. Likely causes of user's observation: slow loading of large uncompressed images (alt text visible until load), viewing an older deployment, or webp unsupported on very old browser.
